newsitem.title: USA: House panel cuts anti-smoking funds in half.
newsitem.headline: House panel cuts anti-smoking funds in half.

text.p: A House panel Wednesday slashed by more than half the Food and Drug Administration's budget for enforcing its new crackdown on youth smoking.

The FDA had requested $34 million, which health officials considered barely enough to get the new program on its feet. But the House Agriculture Appropriations Subcommittee cut the request to $15 million.
"This was the first congressional action on the FDA rule, and the result was very disappointing," said Bill Novelli, president of the Campaign for Tobacco Free Kids.
The FDA rules try to tighten up on sales to teenagers. It requires identification checks of anyone who appears age 27 or younger, and imposes penalties on retailers who sell to young people.

Tobacco sales to minors are illegal in all states, but the bans are unevenly enforced. Anti-smoking groups estimate that teens and children spend more than $1.26 billion of tobacco products each year.

The appropriations move came as health advocates met a few blocks from the Capitol to weigh a proposed settlement between the tobacco industry and state officials. Participants stressed the importance of guaranteeing FDA authority to regulate tobacco. However, that authority also depends on having the funds to take action.
